46: struct ChecksumContext {

48:     bits: usize,
49: }

51: impl ChecksumContext {
52: /// Calculate checksum
53: ///
54: /// # Arguments
55: ///
56: /// * `options` - CLI options for the assigning checksum algorithm
57: /// * `files` - A iterator of OsStr which is a bunch of files that are using for calculating checksum
58: #[allow(clippy::cognitive_complexity)]
59: fn cksum<'a, I>(&self, mut options: Options, files: I) -> UResult<()>
60: where
61:     I: Iterator<Item = &'a OsStr>,
62: {
63:     let files: Vec<_> = files.collect();
64:     if options.output_format == OutputFormat::Raw && files.len() > 1 {
65:         return Err(Box::new(ChecksumError::RawMultipleFiles));
66:     }
67: 
68:     for filename in files {
69:         let filename = Path::new(filename);
70:         let stdin_buf;
71:         let file_buf;
72:         let not_file = filename == OsStr::new("-");
73: 
74:         // Handle the file input
75:         let mut file = BufReader::new(if not_file {
76:             stdin_buf = stdin();
77:             Box::new(stdin_buf) as Box<dyn Read>
78:         } else if filename.is_dir() {
79:             Box::new(BufReader::new(io::empty())) as Box<dyn Read>
80:         } else {
81:             file_buf = match File::open(filename) {
82:                 Ok(file) => file,
83:                 Err(err) => {
84:                     show!(err.map_err_context(|| filename.to_string_lossy().to_string()));
85:                     continue;
86:                 }
87:             };
88:             Box::new(file_buf) as Box<dyn Read>
89:         });
90: 
91:         if filename.is_dir() {
92:             show!(USimpleError::new(
93:                 1,
94:                 format!("{}: Is a directory", filename.display())
95:             ));
96:             continue;
97:         }
98: 
99:         let (sum_hex, sz) =
100:             digest_reader(&mut options.digest, &mut file, false, self.bits)
101:                 .map_err_context(|| "failed to read input".to_string())?;
102: 
103:         let sum = match options.output_format {
104:             OutputFormat::Raw => {
105:                 let bytes = match self.name {
106:                     ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_CRC => sum_hex.parse::<u32>().unwrap().to_be_bytes().to_vec(),
107:                     ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_SYSV | ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_BSD => {
108:                         sum_hex.parse::<u16>().unwrap().to_be_bytes().to_vec()
109:                     }
110:                     _ => hex::decode(sum_hex).unwrap(),
111:                 };
112:                 // Cannot handle multiple files anyway, output immediately.
113:                 stdout().write_all(&bytes)?;
114:                 return Ok(());
115:             }
116:             OutputFormat::Hexadecimal => sum_hex,
117:             OutputFormat::Base64 => match self.name {
118:                 ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_CRC | ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_SYSV | ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_BSD => sum_hex,
119:                 _ => encoding::encode(encoding::Format::Base64, &hex::decode(sum_hex).unwrap())
120:                     .unwrap(),
121:             },
122:         };
123:         // The BSD checksum output is 5 digit integer
124:         let bsd_width = 5;
125:         match (options.algo_name, not_file) {
126:             (ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_SYSV, true) => println!(
127:                 "{} {}",
128:                 sum.parse::<u16>().unwrap(),
129:                 div_ceil(sz, options.output_bits)
130:             ),
131:             (ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_SYSV, false) => println!(
132:                 "{} {} {}",
133:                 sum.parse::<u16>().unwrap(),
134:                 div_ceil(sz, options.output_bits),
135:                 filename.display()
136:             ),
137:             (ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_BSD, true) => println!(
138:                 "{:0bsd_width$} {:bsd_width$}",
139:                 sum.parse::<u16>().unwrap(),
140:                 div_ceil(sz, options.output_bits)
141:             ),
142:             (ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_BSD, false) => println!(
143:                 "{:0bsd_width$} {:bsd_width$} {}",
144:                 sum.parse::<u16>().unwrap(),
145:                 div_ceil(sz, options.output_bits),
146:                 filename.display()
147:             ),
148:             (ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_CRC, true) => println!("{sum} {sz}"),
149:             (ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_CRC, false) => println!("{sum} {sz} {}", filename.display()),
150:             (ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_BLAKE2B, _) if options.tag => {
151:                 if let Some(length) = options.length {
152:                     // Multiply by 8 here, as we want to print the length in bits.
153:                     println!("BLAKE2b-{} ({}) = {sum}", length * 8, filename.display());
154:                 } else {
155:                     println!("BLAKE2b ({}) = {sum}", filename.display());
156:                 }
157:             }
158:             _ => {
159:                 if options.tag {
160:                     println!(
161:                         "{} ({}) = {sum}",
162:                         options.algo_name.to_ascii_uppercase(),
163:                         filename.display()
164:                     );
165:                 } else {
166:                     let prefix = if options.asterisk { "*" } else { " " };
167:                     println!("{sum} {prefix}{}", filename.display());
168:                 }
169:             }
170:         }
171:     }
172: 
173:     Ok(())
174: }
175: }

195: /// Determines whether to prompt an asterisk (*) in the output.
196: ///
197: /// This function checks the `tag`, `binary`, and `had_reset` flags and returns a boolean
198: /// indicating whether to prompt an asterisk (*) in the output.
199: /// It relies on the overrides provided by clap (i.e., `--binary` overrides `--text` and vice versa).
200: /// Same for `--tag` and `--untagged`.
201: fn prompt_asterisk(tag: bool, binary: bool, had_reset: bool) -> bool {
202:     if tag {
203:         return false;
204:     }
205:     if had_reset {
206:         return false;
207:     }
208:     binary
209: }
210: 
211: /**
212:  * Determine if we had a reset.
213:  * This is basically a hack to support the behavior of cksum
214:  * when we have the following arguments:
215:  * --binary --tag --untagged
216:  * Don't do it with clap because if it struggling with the --overrides_with
217:  * marking the value as set even if not present
218:  */
219: fn had_reset(args: &[String]) -> bool {
220:     // Indices where "--binary" or "-b", "--tag", and "--untagged" are found
221:     let binary_index = args.iter().position(|x| x == "--binary" || x == "-b");
222:     let tag_index = args.iter().position(|x| x == "--tag");
223:     let untagged_index = args.iter().position(|x| x == "--untagged");
224: 
225:     // Check if all arguments are present and in the correct order
226:     match (binary_index, tag_index, untagged_index) {
227:         (Some(b), Some(t), Some(u)) => b < t && t < u,
228:         _ => false,
229:     }
230: }
231: 
232: /***
233:  * cksum has a bunch of legacy behavior.
234:  * We handle this in this function to make sure they are self contained
235:  * and "easier" to understand
236:  */
237: fn handle_tag_text_binary_flags(matches: &clap::ArgMatches) -> UResult<(bool, bool)> {
238:     let untagged: bool = matches.get_flag(options::UNTAGGED);
239:     let tag: bool = matches.get_flag(options::TAG);
240:     let tag: bool = tag || !untagged;
241: 
242:     let binary_flag: bool = matches.get_flag(options::BINARY);
243: 
244:     let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
245:     let had_reset = had_reset(&args);
246: 
247:     let asterisk: bool = prompt_asterisk(tag, binary_flag, had_reset);
248: 
249:     Ok((tag, asterisk))
250: }

252: #[uucore::main]
253: pub fn uumain(args: impl uucore::Args) -> UResult<()> {
254:     let matches = uu_app().try_get_matches_from(args)?;
255: 
256:     let check = matches.get_flag(options::CHECK);
257: 
258:     let algo_name: &str = match matches.get_one::<String>(options::ALGORITHM) {
259:         Some(v) => v,
260:         None => {
261:             if check {
262:                 // if we are doing a --check, we should not default to crc
263:                 ""
264:             } else {
265:                 ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_CRC
266:             }
267:         }
268:     };
269: 
270:     if ["bsd", "crc", "sysv"].contains(&algo_name) && check {
271:         return Err(ChecksumError::AlgorithmNotSupportedWithCheck.into());
272:     }
273: 
274:     let input_length = matches.get_one::<usize>(options::LENGTH);
275: 
276:     let length = match input_length {
277:         Some(length) => {
278:             if algo_name == ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_BLAKE2B {
279:                 calculate_blake2b_length(*length)?
280:             } else {
281:                 return Err(ChecksumError::LengthOnlyForBlake2b.into());
282:             }
283:         }
284:         None => None,
285:     };
286: 
287:     if check {
288:         let text_flag = matches.get_flag(options::TEXT);
289:         let binary_flag = matches.get_flag(options::BINARY);
290:         let strict = matches.get_flag(options::STRICT);
291:         let status = matches.get_flag(options::STATUS);
292:         let warn = matches.get_flag(options::WARN);
293:         let ignore_missing = matches.get_flag(options::IGNORE_MISSING);
294:         let quiet = matches.get_flag(options::QUIET);
295: 
296:         if binary_flag || text_flag {
297:             return Err(ChecksumError::BinaryTextConflict.into());
298:         }
299:         // Determine the appropriate algorithm option to pass
300:         let algo_option = if algo_name.is_empty() {
301:             None
302:         } else {
303:             Some(algo_name)
304:         };
305: 
306:         // Execute the checksum validation based on the presence of files or the use of stdin
307: 
308:         let files = matches.get_many::<String>(options::FILE).map_or_else(
309:             || iter::once(OsStr::new("-")).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
310:             |files| files.map(OsStr::new).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
311:         );
312:         return perform_checksum_validation(
313:             files.iter().copied(),
314:             strict,
315:             status,
316:             warn,
317:             binary_flag,
318:             ignore_missing,
319:             quiet,
320:             algo_option,
321:             length,
322:         );
323:     }
324: 
325:     let (tag, asterisk) = handle_tag_text_binary_flags(&matches)?;
326: 
327:     let algo = detect_algo(algo_name, length)?;
328: 
329:     let output_format = if matches.get_flag(options::RAW) {
330:         OutputFormat::Raw
331:     } else if matches.get_flag(options::BASE64) {
332:         OutputFormat::Base64
333:     } else {
334:         OutputFormat::Hexadecimal
335:     };
336: 
337:     let context = ChecksumContext {
338:         name: algo.name,
339:         bits: algo.bits,
340:     };
341:     let opts = Options {
342:         algo_name: algo.name,
343:         digest: (algo.create_fn)(),
344:         output_bits: algo.bits,
345:         length,
346:         tag,
347:         output_format,
348:         asterisk,
349:     };
350: 
351:     match matches.get_many::<String>(options::FILE) {
352:         Some(files) => context.cksum(opts, files.map(OsStr::new))?,
353:         None => context.cksum(opts, iter::once(OsStr::new("-")))?,
354:     };
355: 
356:     Ok(())
357: }

part.text:
Fixed. Changes in `src/uu/cksum/src/cksum.rs`:

1. **Non-UTF-8 args accepted**: the `FILE` arg now uses `value_parser!(OsString)` instead of the default `String` parser, and `get_many` calls use `OsString` (src/uu/cksum/src/cksum.rs:372).
2. **No panic on non-UTF-8 args**: `had_reset` uses `std::env::args_os()` instead of `std::env::args()` (which panics on invalid UTF-8).
3. **Raw filename output**: added `print_line_with_filename` that writes the filename's raw bytes to stdout (via `OsStrExt` on unix) instead of the lossy `Path::display()`, so output matches GNU behavior like `4294967295 0 funky\xffname`.

Verified: `cargo test --test tests cksum` — all 65 cksum tests pass, including the previously failing `test_non_utf8_filename`, and the issue scenario works end-to-end with the `coreutils` binary.
